text: Because the milled curd is never pressed, it settles with tiny airways between the pieces; the sealed surface keeps them closed until steel needles let air in at about six weeks and the Penicillium roqueforti starts veining from the centre. The cheese forms its own crust rather than having one applied.

steps.note: The next day, the curd is cut into pieces the size of walnuts.
The cheese is turned, with no pressure applied.

steps.name: seal
steps.note: The cheese is left to form its own slightly wrinkled coat.
The cheese is pierced with steel needles at about six weeks, so air gets in and the mould veins from the centre.
